html:
The Hupda, who call themselves Hupd'äh, are a forest people of the Vaupés region, on the Tiquié and Papurí rivers on the border of Brazil and Colombia. Their language belongs to the Naduhup family, with those of the Yuhup and the Dâw.

They live inland from the big rivers, hunting and gathering, and move camp often. For a long time they had an unequal tie with the Tukanoan river peoples such as the Desana and Wanano, trading meat and labour for manioc and goods. Missionaries settled many of them in villages in the 1900s.
